The agent drives a real browser with one family of tools: open pages, go back/forward, click, type, pick dropdowns, send keys, scroll, wait, manage tabs, upload files and run page JavaScript.

Merges DOM, accessibility tree and layout into one numbered list of the things a user could click, optionally with a screenshot.

Walks iframes from other origins and routes clicks and reads into the right frame.
Numbered marks on the page (annotate, then act by number)
Draws numbered boxes on clickable elements, in-page or on the screenshot, so the model (and owner) can say 'click 7'.

Picks how the agent drives the browser: DOM tools, pure vision, or both together.

LLM extraction to markdown or structured JSON
Turns the page into clean markdown (chunked for long pages) and asks a model to pull out structured data against a schema.
Web fetch: rendered page to markdown
web.fetch-style reading of a URL through a headless/rendering browser or scrape service, slimmed and converted to markdown.
Reads the current page's main content (Readability) as markdown with offset pagination so long pages don't flood context.
Cheap page search (find text, CSS query)
Non-LLM actions that grep visible page text or query elements by CSS selector without a full extraction.
URLs typed in a message trigger an offer to read them in, with per-URL 'don't ask again'.
The first browser use checks for Playwright/Chromium and installs it (one command), choosing mirrors when needed.
Find and launch a local browser
Locates installed Chrome/Edge/Chromium/Firefox per OS, launches it (local, CDP or cloud engines) and cleans up its processes afterwards.
Event-driven CDP browser session with watchdogs
One browser session object on an event bus, with independent watchdogs for navigation, tabs, downloads and crashes.
CDP target and session pool tracking
Keeps the pool of CDP sessions in sync with attached/detached targets so tabs and popups are never lost.
Hang and crash protection for the browser
Every CDP call has a timeout, crashed targets and stalled requests raise events, and unhealthy browsers are retired instead of hanging the task.
The browser starts only when first needed, is reused by every tool in that conversation/thread and recovers if it was closed.
Browser session cleanup (idle janitor, orphan reaper, tab cleanup)
Closes idle sessions and tabs the agent opened, and kills leaked browser processes on exit.
Long-lived browser sessions that later tasks reuse, renew and reap on timeout, keeping the page and login state between steps.
Named browser profiles (cookies, storage, user-data dir) that are isolated from each other and can be saved, listed, renamed, reset and reused.
Use the owner's real signed-in profile
Snapshot the owner's active Chromium profile into an agent-owned copy so the agent browses with the owner's logins without touching the original.
Attach to a running Chrome over CDP
Discover or launch a debug-port Chrome/Edge/Brave and attach the agent to it (local or remote CDP URL, with headers).
Loads and saves cookies and localStorage to a storage-state file on connect and shutdown.
Read and write cookies / storage as tools
Tools that read and set cookies, localStorage and sessionStorage for logged-in work.
Import cookies and logins from the owner's browser
Copies (decrypting) Chrome-family cookies and profiles into the agent's isolated profile, optionally keeping them in sync.
Merges fresh cookies from each run back into the saved profile, freshest wins, so logins stay alive.
Proxy server, bypass list and proxy auth applied at launch.
Grants configured permissions (clipboard, notifications, geolocation) on connect.
Optionally loads uBlock Origin, a cookie-banner dismisser and ClearURLs into the agent browser.
alert/confirm/prompt dialogs never block the agent: they are captured into a queue the agent answers (or auto-accepted).
Tracks what the browser downloaded (local and remote CDP), sanitises names, auto-saves PDFs and exposes the files.
Wait for page readiness or a condition
Waits for network idle after navigation, or polls until the URL matches a pattern, streaming progress.
A Page/Element/Mouse API for deterministic scripted steps that mixes with AI steps.
Escape-hatch tool that sends any Chrome DevTools Protocol command to the session.
The model gets one tool that runs code against a persistent browser with helpers (tabs, click_at_xy, js, cdp).
A dedicated sub-agent (or planner/navigator/validator trio) handles a browsing task and reports back to the main agent.
An SDK where a page gets AI commands: act('...'), extract, validate, plus AI-assisted click/fill and high-level run_task/login/download helpers.
AI element locator (describe an element in words)
Find an element by describing it; the AI resolves it once, then it behaves like a normal locator.
When an action fails because the page changed, it is rerouted between DOM, accessibility and vision surfaces instead of failing.
The SDK runs its API server in-process so no separate deployment is needed.
Hosted browsers (Browser Use, Browserbase, Firecrawl) on one provider registry, selected by config.
Localhost URLs when the browser is remote
Detects localhost/LAN URLs on a cloud browser and either spawns a local sidecar browser or returns a tunnel hint.
Serve a local browser to the cloud via tunnel
Starts Chrome plus a CDP proxy and optional tunnel so a hosted service can drive a local browser.
Self-hosted fingerprint-spoofing Firefox fork mapped onto the same browser tools.
Opt-in low-memory headless engine for text/DOM tasks with automatic fallback to Chrome.
Opens a visible browser window and keeps headed sessions alive between tasks.
Detects captcha / 'are you human' checks and pauses the step loop until it is solved.
Live browser view with input forwarding
Streams the agent's browser as a live screencast the owner watches and can click, type and scroll in, with tabs, takeover and annotations sent back to the agent.
In-app agent browser (built into the desktop app)
A browser inside the app window that agents drive through tools while the owner watches, with a visible agent cursor and 'agent controlling' chip.
Visual feedback while the agent works: animated cursor, click ripples, highlighted targets and a border marking the page as under agent control.
An overlay blocks the owner's input and shows a banner while the agent acts, lifting only during its own actions.
Records a browser task (rrweb events, MJPEG video with action overlays, or whole-display MP4) for replay and sharing.
Save page as PDF or screenshot
Actions that print the current page to PDF and capture screenshots into the agent's files.
Page snapshot diffs (watch a page for change)
Takes successive snapshots of a tab and diffs them under a deadline, plus screenshots and PDFs of the page.
Ask a vision model about the page
Takes an (optionally annotated) screenshot and answers a question about it with a vision model.
Lists the images on the current page (src, alt) for follow-up analysis, SSRF-guarded.
Returns page console output and evaluates JavaScript in the page.
Every navigation, redirect, snapshot, console and eval path is checked against private/loopback addresses, with a denylist of sensitive JS primitives.
Config sets a default plus per-origin allow/deny policy (and history access) for the agent's browser.
Managed requirements for the in-app browser
Admin-managed requirements for the interactive in-app browser, such as whether external sites are allowed.
Oversized trees are truncated (full copy saved to a file), secrets are redacted before reaching the model and typed text is redacted in logs.
The owner acknowledges a privacy notice before the browser agent is first used.
Fills saved usernames, passwords and OTP codes into page fields by handle from a local vault, so the model never sees the secret; only on allowed origins.
Shows 1Password/pass entries as metadata only and delivers a secret by a confirmed, expiring clipboard copy.
Detects OTP inputs split across several boxes and types the code digit by digit.
Drive the owner's own Chrome tabs via an extension
A Chrome extension (chrome.debugger) plus an authenticated local relay lets the agent drive tabs the owner shares in his signed-in browser, with per-tab pause/allow.
One browser action routes each call to whichever target is available: the extension, the embedded browser, a headless fallback or a remote server.
Extension screenshot and file upload channel
A one-shot, time-limited upload channel for screenshots and files from the extension, with size and type caps.
The desktop controller holds identity keys in the OS credential store and exchanges encrypted, signed browser commands with remote devices.
When no real browser is available, browser commands run against JSDOM.
Injects the live tab list and dispatch mode into the agent's context when browsing.
Older page snapshots in history are replaced with short placeholders so only the latest stays in context.
Seeded minimum-jerk pointer paths that land inside the target, instead of teleporting.
Interactive task lifecycle with revalidated actuation
Each step of an interactive task is persisted before dispatch and re-checked (page, frame, input revision, policy) at the moment of the click, so stale approvals are refused.
Runs the browser inside a sandbox container network and lets the owner watch/take over through an authenticated noVNC link.
One shared definition of browser action limits and timeouts used by both the tool schema and the runtime.
Settings/CLI flags for the browser: CDP endpoint, executable, headless, proxy, user agent, user-data dir, viewport, provider.
Discord account scraper over the browser
Per-account Discord scraper over a browser CDP session, exposed as a service.
A browser extension streams page, video progress, subtitles and frames from video sites to the agent.
Owner browser controls (address bar, search, back/forward/reload, Stop/Pause, truthful states, Chrome extras)

The owner-facing browser chrome: type an address or search words, back/forward/reload, Stop and Pause, honest loading/refused/failed states, IME/clipboard/selection, find-in-page, zoom, history and bookmarks, and an owner window not bound by per-task limits.
Branch browser view layout (full-size view, docked chat, PiP, Trunk naming)
Branch's own look for the browser: full-size view with the conversation docked, picture-in-picture, a globe button in the header, no separate Browser tab, named for its Trunk with its face.
keepoak.com opens in Branch's browser view as a locked session of its own; the agent can't act there unless allowed.

Screenshots black out password boxes before any picture reaches a model or the owner's log.
A named multi-page journey with one picture per step, saved and run again in one step.
Remember a site's quirks (cookie notice to press, what to wait for) with a Settings list and Forget.
Always pick the most private choice (decline non-essential) on any site, e.g. via DuckDuckGo autoconsent in opt-out mode.
A per-site opt-in lets scheduled tasks use a saved sign-in, with an owner recovery step when it fails.
Hand to the owner for password changes, captchas and security warnings; confirm camera/mic/location prompts and downloads; optional confirm-every-type and block-uploads switches.
Read the owner's browser history only with approval and within a date range.
Learn a site's API from network traffic
Capture a site's network traffic and turn it into an API skill so later tasks skip the browser.

Requirements filed under browser that are about desktop computer use.

All apps: gateway runs every chat app in one background process
One long-running gateway starts each enabled chat app, relays messages to agent sessions and sends replies back, and keeps answering while the window is closed. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: channel plugin SDK and adapter contract

A public contract for writing one chat-app adapter: inbound context, ingress authorization, outbound adapters with receipts, durable sends and live previews, so every app gets the same behaviours. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: ordered message pipeline stages
Every inbound message passes ordered stages (wake, allowlist, session status, rate limit, safety, preprocess, process, decorate, respond) that can wrap later stages.
All apps: supervised gateway process with auto-restart
Chat adapters run in a supervised child process with a ready signal and restart with exponential backoff, so one crash does not take chat apps down.
All apps: reconnect with a needs-attention status

Disconnected adapters reconnect in the background (also after sleep/wake) and, past a failure threshold, are flagged as needing attention with the reason shown, instead of retrying silently forever. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: enable, disable, pause or reload one chat app live
Turning a chat app on, off or reconfiguring it (or pausing a failing one with /platform from chat) starts or stops only that adapter inside the running gateway.
All apps: single gateway per user (attach instead of a second copy)
A host lock plus rendezvous record lets later launches attach to, rescan or replace the live gateway instead of binding a second port.
All apps: restart-complete notice to the requesting chat
After a restart the gateway tells the chat (and thread) that asked for it that it is back, including how long it took.
All apps: auto-resume turns cut off by a restart
Turns interrupted by a gateway restart are marked and continued automatically after boot if still fresh, never twice.
All apps: relay adapter for platforms fronted by a remote connector
One generic adapter takes a capability descriptor at handshake and lets a remote connector own the platform wire, so a relay machine can hold the chat accounts.
All apps: relay egress target authorization
Messages sent through the relay are refused unless the gateway has a record of that destination, so the model cannot address arbitrary chats.
All apps: hosted multi-tenant webhook gateway
A hosted gateway verifies connector webhooks, routes each event to the owning agent and delivers replies for many tenants.
All apps: one public webhook URL for every webhook-based app
Webhook-based adapters (Slack HTTP, LINE, WeCom, QQ, Lark, Teams, SMS) share one listener under per-bot or per-profile paths instead of opening their own ports.
All apps: DM pairing codes for unknown senders

A stranger who DMs the bot gets a short one-time code (unambiguous alphabet, expiry, rate-limited, lockout on failed approvals); the owner approves it and the sender is added for that app. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: unauthorized senders get a code or silence, owner gets one notice
Strangers either receive a pairing code or total silence when an allowlist exists (so the bot is not revealed), and the owner gets one sanitized notice per sender explaining the fix.
All apps: DM access policy (open, allowlist, pairing, disabled)
Each app has a DM policy and a group policy chosen from open, allowlist, pairing or disabled, with per-scope allow lists. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: sender and group allowlists (one global list plus per-app lists)

Allowlists of users and groups (exact ids, wildcards, group names/keywords) gate who may talk to the bot, read per profile and fail closed; a nickname blocklist drops named users. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: bind a chat account as the owner
A pairing command (e.g. /pair with a 6-digit code) binds a chat user as the owner, and the backend can DM the owner by id; sender authority is resolved per message.
All apps: command permission tiers (owner/admin vs everyone)
A second access axis decides who may run which slash commands, separately for DMs and groups, with a /help and /whoami floor for others.
All apps: confirm destructive slash commands
Destructive commands such as session reset ask for an explicit confirm (buttons where supported, text otherwise) before running.
All apps: cap on concurrently active chat sessions
An optional limit on simultaneously active chat sessions; new conversations beyond it get a polite rejection.
All apps: hide raw user and chat ids from the model
User and chat identifiers can be hashed in the model-visible session context where raw ids are not needed.
All apps: bot-to-bot reply loop guard
A budget on bot-authored messages per conversation plus a 'this is a bot' hint stops two agents from replying to each other forever. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: ignore the bot's own echoes
Messages the bot just sent (or its own account's messages) are not processed as new input.
A fixed-window limit per chat either waits for the next window or drops the extra messages.
The bot answers only between configured start and stop times.
All apps: ignore messages by prefix or pattern
Messages starting with configured prefixes or matching patterns are dropped silently.
All apps: mute or switch off the agent in one chat
Mute a room or a whole server (optionally for a time that auto-expires), set a reply gate (mention-only, muted until a lift phrase), or disable a session entirely.
A group can switch individual plugins off for itself.
All apps: human takeover of a room
The agent stops replying while a human has taken over a room and resumes when handed back.
All apps: group trigger rules (mention, reply, prefix, keyword, pattern)

In groups the agent answers only when mentioned, replied to, or triggered by a configured prefix, keyword or pattern (stripped before processing), with a per-group 'every message / only when mentioned' activation the owner can set from chat. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: bare mention asks what the person wants
A message that only mentions the bot gets a short 'what can I do?' and the next message is treated as addressed.
All apps: work out who a group message is addressed to
Classifies, without a model call, whether a message addresses the agent, someone else or nobody, and records addressing edges.
All apps: talk less when dominating a group
Live signals (the agent's share of recent turns, who talks to whom, pace) make the agent hold back in busy groups; includes a When2Speak evaluation.
All apps: occasional unprompted replies in groups
In chosen groups the bot may reply to unaddressed messages with a set probability or a decaying attention score.
All apps: listen to unmentioned group messages as quiet context
Unmentioned group chatter is recorded as context (with sender names and media) so the next mention knows what was said, without the bot replying.
All apps: follow-ups in threads the bot already joined
Threads the bot has replied in are remembered, so follow-ups there are answered without a fresh mention.
All apps: say who is speaking in shared group sessions
In shared group sessions each message is prefixed with the sender's name so the agent knows who is talking.
All apps: introduction when added to a group
When the bot joins a group (or a user subscribes) it posts one configurable introduction grounded in the room's title and description.
All apps: session keys per chat, thread, topic and user

One deterministic builder gives each DM, group member, thread or topic its own conversation (or a shared one by choice), persisted across restarts with readable aliases. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: route each chat, group, topic or thread to a chosen agent

Bindings by peer, parent, guild, team, roles, account or channel pick which agent answers each conversation (most specific wins), with a trace of why; the owner's DMs on every app can share one main conversation with the window. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: several bot accounts per app, each bound to its own agent
One gateway runs several bot accounts of the same app (e.g. two Telegram bots), each with its own credentials and owning agent.
All apps: per-channel model and system prompt overrides
A channel or thread can pin its own model, system prompt additions and auto-loaded skills, between a session override and the global default.
Per-channel hooks adjust run parameters after they are resolved (e.g. Feishu, GitHub).
All apps: continuity hint after a session reset
After a reset in a long-lived channel, the agent gets a note pointing at the previous session so it can recall it.
All apps: messages that arrive while busy: queue, interrupt or steer

Messages sent while the agent is working are queued, interrupt the run, or are steered into it, per setting; control commands (/stop, /approve) always get through. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: read receipts for queued follow-ups
Follow-up messages drained mid-turn still get their read-receipt reactions.
All apps: /cancel that bypasses the queue
/cancel is handled before queueing and stops the chat's running turn at once.
All apps: skip messages a newer turn already superseded
Out-of-order inbound messages are tagged, skipped or ignored so the agent does not answer something a newer turn replaced.
All apps: in-chat slash commands from one command catalog
Commands such as /new, /reset, /status, /model, /stop, /help work inside every chat app from one shared catalog. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: session idle reset and max age
The owner chooses when a chat's conversation resets: after an idle period or a maximum age, per thread.
All apps: wait for messages split in two (inbound debounce)
Bursts of short messages from the same chat (and long pastes the app split) are merged into one turn after a quiet window, keeping order. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: drop redelivered and duplicate inbound messages
A bounded cache (in-process or shared SQL across pods) of seen message ids drops platform retries and duplicate events, including Slack unfurl duplicates.
All apps: suppress a duplicate reply to the same message
An identical second reply to the same inbound message is dropped.
All apps: photos, files and voice notes in, with size limits
Inbound attachments are downloaded with byte and time caps, cached safely, inlined as model input (images, documents) and can wait to join the follow-up question. Applies to every connected chat app.
Allowed URLs in messages (including hidden link targets) are fetched with limits and summarized into context.
All apps: quoted message added to context
When someone replies to an earlier message, the quoted message is fetched and added so the agent sees what is referenced.
All apps: message timestamps in model context
Inbound messages carry a readable timestamp in the model context without changing what is stored.
All apps: platform chat and sender context
Room metadata and sender identity (handles, aliases, account labels) are injected separately from the transcript.
Shared pins, venues and live locations become text the agent can use; outbound locations are sent where supported (Telegram, others).
All apps: reactions, edits, joins and pokes reach the agent
Non-message events (reactions on the bot's messages, edits, membership changes, QQ pokes, friend requests) are normalized, authorized and delivered to the agent and plugins.
All apps: edited messages are answered in their newest version
When the person edits a message before or during the reply, the newest version supersedes the old one (Telegram edits, Discord MESSAGE_UPDATE, Slack message_changed, Matrix edits).
The agent can send native polls (Telegram, Matrix, Teams Adaptive Cards) and read the results.
All apps: native formatting per app from one Markdown model

Replies are parsed once into text plus style/link spans and rendered natively per app (Telegram HTML, Slack mrkdwn, Signal ranges, Matrix HTML, WhatsApp), with a plain-text fallback, chosen live per app. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: long replies split at paragraph breaks, code fences never broken
Long replies go out as several messages at paragraph or sentence boundaries within each app's limit, merging tiny blocks and never leaving a code block open. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: very long replies as an image or merged-forward message
Replies over a threshold are rendered to an image or folded into a merged-forward message (QQ) to avoid flooding.
All apps: human-like pauses between message parts
Multi-part replies can be split and sent with natural or random delays so they read like typing.
All apps: portable message cards (buttons, selects, forms, charts, tables)
One semantic presentation (cards, buttons, selects, forms, follow-ups, charts, tables) is rendered natively by each app or degraded to text within limits. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: clarify questions as buttons with a text fallback

When the agent asks the person to choose, options appear as native buttons (Telegram, Discord, Slack); any failure falls back to a numbered text list, and expiry is handled. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: answer a question by reacting with a number
On apps without buttons (WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage) people answer a 1-4 option question by reacting with a number emoji.
All apps: tool approvals in chat, with /approve and /deny fallback

Risky actions ask in the chat with shared wording (what, why, silence means no) as native buttons bound to the request, or /approve and /deny where there are no buttons; only authorized people can answer. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: approvals by emoji reaction
On WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix an approval is answered by reacting, limited to the requester.
All apps: model picker in chat
/model opens a picker (provider, then model) as Telegram inline keyboards, Discord select menus or Slack Block Kit menus, and the choice is saved per chat.
All apps: send files and images back as native attachments

Files the agent makes (charts, PDFs, audio, images) are sent as native attachments after a path safety check, from MEDIA tags or bare paths in the reply, including files on a remote sandbox. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: expiring file links for platforms that fetch by URL
Local files are served under expiring tokens so platforms and TTS can fetch media by URL.
All apps: usage footer on replies
An optional footer (model, context use, latency) on final replies, per app, toggled with /footer.
When the agent's whole answer is a silence marker, nothing is sent while history still records the turn.
All apps: quote-reply and @-mention the sender
Replies quote the message they answer (with a first/all/off mode for multi-part answers) and can @-mention the sender in groups; optional reply prefix/suffix. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: choose what reaches the chat (progress, tool hints, reasoning)
Global and per-app switches decide whether progress, tool hints, model reasoning and compaction notices are shown in chat apps.
All apps: diagnostics kept apart from answers
Engine warnings and service notices are classified separately so chats can mute or route them without hiding real replies.
All apps: what the person sees when a turn fails
On errors the chat gets a configurable hint, the error, or nothing.
All apps: notices that delete themselves
Short system notices are deleted after a time on apps that allow deleting messages.
All apps: replies stream into one message, edited in place

The answer streams into a single message that is edited at a throttled rate (or a native draft/stream where the app has one), with fences closed in previews, think blocks hidden, overflow split and no duplicate final. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: one progress message with step lines, edited in place

While working, one quiet message shows the status line and tool steps (with per-app level: off/new/all/verbose), rolls to a new message when too long, and the answer is its own message; SMS gets none and phone-first apps get a summary line. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: remove progress messages once the answer lands
Opt-in deletion of tool-progress messages after the final reply so the chat keeps only the answer.
All apps: friendly status phrases for long turns
Long turns show short human status lines from a catalog the owner can extend, never quoting tool arguments.
If a running turn shows no activity for a while, the chat gets a stall notice that clears when work resumes.
One pinned message, edited in place, shows the agent's tasks and plan as a sidebar substitute (Telegram /tasks, Slack summaries).
All apps: typing indicator while working
The app's typing indicator is shown and refreshed during a turn, with modes and a timeout so a stuck turn does not type forever. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: status reactions on the person's message
An acknowledgement emoji on receipt, then reactions that cycle queued, thinking, tool, done or error (tapbacks on iMessage). Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: bot presence shows health
The bot's online status shows healthy, degraded or rate-limited so people can see when the agent is unavailable.

Inbound events are journaled before they are acknowledged, drained in order with retries and ownership claims, and dead letters can be inspected and resubmitted, so nothing is lost or handled twice. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: durable delivery ledger for replies

Each reply is recorded pending, attempting, delivered or failed; a crash before the app confirms redelivers it in order, ambiguous resends are marked, dead letters can be retried, and a turn ends when delivery is confirmed. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: retry sends with backoff
Failed sends retry on a backoff ladder (honouring Retry-After) but stop on errors marked permanent.
All apps: catch up on messages missed while offline
After downtime the gateway finds messages sent meanwhile (history scan or persisted cursor), deduplicates them and answers once, while an age fence suppresses stale backlog.
Chats proven unreachable (bot removed, group deleted) are skipped by scheduled delivery until a later send succeeds.
All apps: send, edit, react and delete across apps (message tool)

One agent tool lists targets and sends text or files to any connected chat, edits or deletes its own earlier messages, reacts, pins and reads channels; scripts can post too. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: directory of reachable chats
The gateway keeps a refreshed map of reachable channels and contacts with friendly names, used to resolve targets.
All apps: home channel and delivery targets for scheduled output
Scheduled and background output goes to an explicit chat, the app's home channel (/sethome), the origin chat or a file, landing in the right thread; friendly aliases and email delivery included.
All apps: record what was sent into the target chat's history
When the agent sends into another chat, that chat's transcript records it so the agent there knows.
All apps: wake the chat when background work finishes
Background processes and delegations resume the owning chat session when they complete.
All apps: escalate to the owner across apps until acknowledged
An unacknowledged message escalates to the owner across ordered channels with retries until seen.
All apps: draft a reply and hand it to the owner for approval
The agent drafts a reply to a chosen message and sends it at once or holds it for owner approval.
All apps: install a messenger into a workspace and push into chats
Install the bot into Slack, Discord, Telegram or WeChat workspaces via OAuth or link tokens and push resources into chats.
All apps: pair a device from chat
/pair in chat creates a setup code for the phone app and lets the owner approve pending devices; the desktop hosts a hub phones connect to by QR.
All apps: guided setup with credential checks
Each app has an in-window setup: credential fields, live validation with clear progress and errors, and enable switches. Applies to every connected chat app.
All apps: chat apps from the command line
Commands to list, configure, start, stop and log in to chat apps (including QR logins) with schema-checked config and secret redaction.
All apps: bot list with per-bot logs and status
Create, enable and disable bots and read each bot's own log; the owner can ask for connector status from chat.
All apps: one-click app creation by QR (Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeCom)
Instead of copying app ids and secrets, the owner scans a QR code and the platform app is created and its credentials filled in.
All apps: QR login for phone-linked accounts (WhatsApp, WeChat)
Interactive QR login sessions shown in the window (with steps, connected and error states) that save credentials when the scan completes.
All apps: third-party chat frontends authenticate as a client app
Registered client apps act for a user identified by a phone number verified by OTP.
All apps: synthetic QA channel for testing
A deterministic fake channel lets automated tests drive the real channel plugin boundary with inspectable state.
All apps: several agents answer in one group
One group message can fan out to several configured agents, each in its own session, selected by mention, with a bounded number of follow-up rounds and names shown on replies.
All apps: channel doctor, probe and security audit
Per-app health checks probe credentials and connectivity, list status issues with fixes, and audit the app's security settings (open DMs, wildcard allowlists).
All apps: remember sent messages so replies to them keep context
A local index of what the bot sent (and WhatsApp received) by message id lets a reply to an earlier rich message recover its text and attachments, which Telegram and WhatsApp do not echo back.
All apps: hand a window conversation off to a chat app
/handoff moves the current conversation to a chat app (Telegram, Discord) so it continues there.
Telegram bot over polling or webhook with photos, video, voice, documents, locations, reply context, proxy support and per-chat state.
Telegram: durable polling, single poller and liveness watchdog

Long polling runs in a worker that spools every update durably before acknowledging it, keeps the read position per bot (surviving update renumbering), holds a single-poller lease per token, handles 409 conflicts and rebuilds on stalls; the after-restart backlog is marked as catch-up.
Updates arrive through a gateway-hosted webhook instead of polling, refusing updates without a secret token.
Telegram: flood control and send pacing
A per-chat one-per-second budget paces sends and edits (interim edits skipped, finals never), waits out retry_after, backs off on 5xx, and edits more slowly in groups.
Telegram: network fallback when the API host is unreachable
When api.telegram.org cannot be reached, requests retry known IPv4 addresses with the hostname kept, using DNS-over-HTTPS discovery.
Telegram: live draft streaming and progress drafts
Replies stream into a preview message (or Telegram's native sendMessageDraft in DMs) in off/partial/block/progress modes, so only the final message notifies.
Telegram: forum topics and DM topics as separate chats
Each forum topic (and bot DM topic via /topic) is its own session, with topic create/rename, model-generated topic names, persisted bindings and pruning.
In groups the bot answers when @mentioned, replied to, addressed by /cmd@bot (ignoring /cmd@otherbot) or in free-response topics; reply chains in normal groups stay one conversation.
The '/' menu is filled from the command list per scope (default, private, groups, owner DM) within Telegram's limits, refreshed only when changed; /start gets a proper welcome.
Typing @bot <query> in any chat searches every command and skill with paging; tapping one sends it.
Telegram: rich formatting (HTML, tables, task lists, math)
Markdown becomes Telegram HTML, with tables, task lists, details and math sent as rich blocks where available and plain-text fallback.
Approvals show as inline buttons (once, session, always, deny) bound to the request; clicks are authorization-checked and fail closed.
Telegram: photo albums read as one message
Photos sent as an album, with their captions, become one message to the agent.
Telegram: photos, files and documents in and out
Inbound documents and images are cached with size limits (large images compressed); outbound photos go as photos and documents up to 50 MB as files.
Incoming stickers (including animated) are described once by a vision model and cached; sticker packs can be added.
Telegram: voice bubbles versus audio files
Spoken replies go out as native voice-note bubbles with duration; other audio as files; inbound voice notes are cached for transcription.
/dashboard in a DM opens the full control UI inside Telegram as a Mini App, owner-checked from Telegram's signed init data.
Telegram: follow a group upgraded to a supergroup
When a group migrates to a supergroup (migrate_to_chat_id), bindings, allowlists and sessions move to the new chat id.
Telegram: read-only history from a personal account
Identity-verified personal Telegram clients serve read-only chat history with owner policy checked per page.
Discord bot for servers and DMs with channel gating, bot-to-bot policy, forwarded messages, attachments, reply-to and typing.

Commands and skills register as Discord application commands with argument menus, synced by fingerprint with rate-limit pacing and role checks, including a model picker that remembers per-user choices.
A channel message can start a thread named by the model; each thread is its own conversation and bindings persist.
Discord: mention gating and free-response channels
In servers the bot needs a mention (also inside threads) except in free-response channels; ignored and no-thread channels are configurable.
Discord: Components v2 buttons, selects and modals
Agent messages use Discord components (buttons, selects, modals, embeds) and interactions route back to the agent.
An 'Open widget' button launches an agent-made HTML widget inside a Discord Activity, gated by Discord OAuth.
A reply streams into one Discord message edited as chunks arrive, never splitting surrogate pairs.
Approvals render as Discord button views (once, session, always, deny), can mention the owner, and accept clicks only from authorized users.
Access can be granted by Discord role or username, resolved to ids and reloaded live.
Outbound messages block @everyone, @here and role pings by default.
Discord: long messages, escaping and forum posts
Long replies split losslessly under Discord's cap (code fences, surrogates), markdown is escaped, and replies to forum channels create forum posts.
Inbound images, audio and documents are downloaded with size caps; files go out as attachments.
Discord: gateway liveness and close-code handling
Health comes from the gateway socket's heartbeat state; fatal close codes stop with a plain card (e.g. turn on Message Content intent), zombies RESUME, and REST rate limits are kept per bucket.
Discord: server management and moderation actions
Gated actions create/edit channels, categories and roles, set permissions, assign roles, create invites and moderate (timeouts, kicks, bans).
Proxied PluralKit messages resolve to the real member so allowlists and identity work for plural systems.
Agent audio is sent as a native Discord voice message with waveform and duration.
Discord: voice channel join, listen and talk
The bot joins a voice channel, transcribes each speaker separately and plays spoken replies, with idle timeouts.
Discord: use the desktop app without a bot token
Connects to the local Discord desktop app over RPC to read messages and reply through UI automation.
Slack app for channels, DMs and threads with ingress and bot policies, thread replies, user-mention resolution and reaction acknowledgement.
Slack: Socket Mode, HTTP and relay transports with a watchdog
Connects by Socket Mode, HTTP request URLs, or a relay that owns the single socket and forwards typed events; a watchdog restarts stale sockets.
Replies stream through Slack's native streaming API as one message that becomes the final reply.
Slack: Block Kit and mrkdwn rendering
Replies render as Block Kit (headers, lists, buttons, selects) or mrkdwn with code kept exact; text fallback when blocks are rejected; <!channel>/<!here> made inert.
Chart and table blocks map to Slack's native data-visualization and table blocks.
Slack: assistant status, task cards and Agent View
In Slack's AI pane the bot shows live 'is thinking' status, per-tool progress or task cards, thread titles and suggested prompts; each composer message starts its own thread session.
Slack: thread context and proactive posts
When pulled into a thread the bot reads earlier thread messages; it can also post proactively to configured targets or feeds.
Slack: channel mention rules and DM policy
Channels answer on mention, mention-or-reply or everything, with group allowlists, and a separate DM policy that issues pairing codes.
Slack: approval buttons and model picker
Approvals and model choice post as Block Kit buttons/menus that only authorized users can use, updated in place.
Slack file attachments are downloaded (restricted to Slack hosts) and agent files uploaded back to the thread.
Slack: start a turn by reacting
Users can start a turn by reacting with chosen emoji.
Raw <@U...> mentions become readable names and the bot knows which one is itself.
Slack modals collect structured input and global/message shortcuts start agent actions; submitted values are summarized for the agent.
Org-wide installs resolve the right workspace and user for each event.
Slack: slash command and App Home
A Slack slash command (with argument menus) starts or steers sessions; !cmd works in threads; a safe App Home tab.
Slack: post as a real user
Optionally read and post as the human who authorized the app, or override display name and icon.
When a recent participant comes online the agent may send one short, memory-informed greeting with a long cooldown.
WhatsApp: personal number by QR (linked device)
Links a personal WhatsApp account as a linked device by QR, then sends and receives text, voice and media, quote-replies and handles LID identities.
WhatsApp: connection controller (reconnect, relink on logout)
Owns the socket lifecycle with reconnect backoff and credential persistence; 'logged out' or 'replaced by another session' asks to relink instead of looping.
Official WhatsApp Business webhooks with signature checks and Graph API sends.
WhatsApp: one identity for LID and phone ids
A person seen as a LID or a phone JID maps to one identifier so allowlists and sessions stay consistent.
WhatsApp: group activation and mention gating
Groups answer on mention or reply to the bot (or always, per group) with group allowlists and a one-time introduction.
Signal through a signal-cli daemon (JSON-RPC and SSE) with attachments, reactions, typing, quotes, groups and account-conflict detection.
Signal: signal-cli install, daemon and transports
Installs signal-cli if missing and supervises its daemon (QR-linked or registered number), or uses a REST container or UNIX socket, auto-detected.
Markdown becomes Signal text-style ranges (bold, italic, monospace) with long replies chunked without breaking styles and wide tables shown as key-value lines.
A token bucket mirrors Signal's per-account attachment limit and recalibrates from Retry-After.
Group messages are processed only when the bot is mentioned (configurable), with a separate lane for commands.
iMessage: on the Messages Mac (chat.db / imsg)
Reads Messages on the Mac (Full Disk Access) and sends replies, with contacts resolved and group/DM policies; blocked on Windows and Linux with the Mac prerequisites stated.
iMessage: from a non-Mac through BlueBubbles
iMessage through a BlueBubbles server on a Mac: REST sends, webhook inbound with media, typing and read receipts.
iMessage through hosted services: signed webhooks or a supervised sidecar stream, with device-code setup.
iMessage: tapbacks, effects, threaded replies and groups
With the private API the agent sends threaded replies, tapbacks, effects, polls and attachment replies and manages groups.
iMessage: approvals by poll or tapback
Approval requests show as iMessage polls or tapback prompts and resolve from the vote or reaction.
Any homeserver with E2EE, cross-signing bootstrap, recovery keys, device verification and key-backup health; supervises bridge bots.
Matrix threads are their own sessions with thread relations on replies; rooms answer on mention, open or allowlist.
Replies and steps stream by editing one m.notice (m.replace) and only the final edit notifies.
Markdown renders to Matrix HTML including tables, code and spoilers.
Room invites are accepted by policy so the bot can be added without manual joins.
Matrix: voice messages wait for the mention
Unmentioned voice messages in mention-gated rooms wait until the sender's follow-up mention claims them.
Teams DMs, group chats and channels through a Bot Framework webhook with token verification, in-thread replies, history, media and reactions.
Approvals render as Adaptive Cards and resolve from card submits.
Teams: file uploads by consent card
Files go to users via Teams' file-consent card in DMs and via Graph/SharePoint elsewhere; inbound attachments come through Graph.
Stored conversation references let the agent message Teams users and channels proactively.
Replies use Teams' streaming message protocol with full-redelivery fallback.
Teams: meeting summaries posted to Teams
The meeting pipeline posts meeting summaries through the same Teams app.
Google Chat app for DMs and spaces via signed HTTP webhooks or Pub/Sub, with Cards v2 replies, threads, attachments and reactions.
Google Chat: native attachments via per-user OAuth
Each user grants OAuth once so the bot can upload native attachments as that user.
Approvals show as Google Chat cards with buttons, updated when resolved.
Feishu/Lark bots for DMs and groups over WebSocket or encrypted webhook, with mention-gated groups, allowlists, per-chat serial processing, media and custom domains.
Replies stream into a CardKit card (typewriter effect, collapsible reasoning, tables split to card limits), falling back to a normal message.
Feishu/Lark: processing reactions and card approvals
Typing and failure reactions on messages; card-button approvals arrive as events.
Comments mentioning the bot on Feishu docs trigger the agent, which replies in the comment thread under per-document rules.
Feishu/Lark: document, drive, wiki and permission tools
Agent tools to create and edit Feishu docs from Markdown (batch inserts, tables), and work with Drive, Wiki and sharing permissions.
An invitation to a Feishu meeting becomes a message so the reply reaches the inviter.
Each run renders as a card with status header, collapsible thinking and tool panels, elapsed time and cancellation state.
Feishu/Lark: markdown cards with inline images
Non-streamed markdown replies go as rich cards and markdown image links are uploaded so they render inline.
Feishu/Lark: recalling a message cancels its run
When a user recalls a message, its queued turn is dropped or its running turn cancelled.
DingTalk robot via Stream Mode (no public IP) for private and group chats with markdown, images, files and interactive status/question cards.
Replies stream into DingTalk AI cards from a template, disabling themselves on failure.
Acts through an existing DingTalk Workspace CLI login for DMs, groups and document mentions.
WeCom: AI bot (long connection or webhook) with streaming
WeCom intelligent bot over a long connection or encrypted webhook with streamed replies, media, template-card buttons, feedback events and welcome messages.
Self-built WeCom apps receive AES-encrypted callbacks, ack at once and reply later through the app API.
Handles WeChat KF callbacks by syncing messages with a persisted cursor and replying to external WeChat users.
WeCom: per-chat send queue with a control lane
Per-chat queues respect WeCom's 30 messages/minute limit while approvals and final frames are never starved.
Inbound attachments are cached; outbound image/video/voice/file use chunked upload.
Personal WeChat via iLink long-poll with QR login, persisted tokens, context tokens, AES media, typing and deferred retries; WeChatPad as an alternative.
WeChat: block streaming for an app without edits
Long replies flush as blocks of a few messages and progress messages are capped.
WeChat: Official Account (passive window or active send)
Official accounts answer within WeChat's 5-second passive window (deduping retries) or reply later through the customer-service API.
QQ through OneBot v11 implementations with group/private messages, files, faces, merged forwards and per-group reply rules.
QQ official bot over WebSocket or Ed25519-signed webhook for C2C, group and guild messages with markdown and media.
Files over 10 MB upload in parallel parts with retries and daily-quota handling.
Replies stream into QQ's stream message API.
Approvals render as QQ inline keyboard buttons whose events map back to the decision.
Tencent Yuanbao bot over WebSocket with auth binding, heartbeat, reconnect and SSRF-guarded media.
A sticker catalogue lets the agent send native Yuanbao stickers.
KOOK WebSocket client with heartbeat, resume, card messages and role cache.
LINE webhooks (signature-verified, spooled durably) with text, media, locations, templates and quick replies.
LINE: free reply tokens with slow-answer button
Uses free reply tokens first; for slow turns spends the token on a button whose tap delivers the cached answer.
Presentations, code and tables become LINE Flex cards within byte limits; selects become quick replies.
Mattermost over WebSocket and REST with thread or flat replies, thread context, modes (on mention, on message, on prefix), allowlists, reactions and pairing.
Native Mattermost slash commands and interactive buttons including a model picker and question answers.
Satori protocol client bridging any Satori-compatible platform.
Responds to Misskey mentions and chat messages with default note visibility.
IRC: channel with TLS and NickServ
Joins IRC channels and DMs over TLS with NickServ, mention-triggered replies, allowlists and line-length splitting.
Signs in as a Twitch bot, joins channels, replies with access control and token refresh.
Talks to a SimpleX daemon, auto-accepts contacts (configurable) and allowlists by contact id.
Subscribes to an ntfy topic and publishes replies to a topic.
Home Assistant: state changes as messages
State-change events become agent messages and replies are posted as notifications.
Self-hosted Nextcloud Talk webhook bot with signed requests, durable spool, reactions and Markdown.
Synology Chat outgoing webhook for inbound DMs paired with an incoming webhook for replies and files.
Answers Tlon DMs and group mentions over an Urbit ship with threads, rich text and images.
Zalo bots for DMs and groups via long polling or webhook with durable spooling.
Automates a personal Zalo account with QR login and per-chat queues.
Receives and answers encrypted Nostr DMs over configured relays with catch-up.
Publishes the bot's Nostr profile from config or the UI.
Joins Buzz workspace relays with authenticated WebSocket, mention and pubkey gating, signed replies, threads and catch-up.
Raft sends authenticated wake hints and the agent reads and sends messages with the Raft CLI.
Manages peer agents with a trust store so only approved peers can exchange messages.
Self-hosted ClickClack workspace bot with realtime WebSocket, setup codes, mention gating and command menu.
Socket.IO client with polling fallback, cursor persistence and per-group mention rules.
@mentions in Linear issues start agent sessions with progress posted as activities; OAuth install and webhooks included.
People email the agent: IMAP is polled, replies go out via SMTP with In-Reply-To threading and attachments in and out; processed mail is marked only after handling.
Inbound mail counts as from a sender only if the receiving server's Authentication-Results show aligned DKIM and SPF pass, so forged From lines cannot pose as the owner.
SMS/MMS through a signature-validated Twilio webhook with durable spool, replies via the Messages API, delivery status and markdown stripped.
SMS: Android phone as SMS gateway
An Android app forwards inbound texts to the local agent, sends multipart SMS with receipts and reads SMS threads.
Polls X DMs with a durable cursor so restarts never double-reply; one client per X account.
Posts on an interval, answers mentions, and likes, reposts, quotes or follows from timeline and search, honouring dry-run.
Publish, read and search public feeds on X, Bluesky, Farcaster, Nostr and Instagram, kept separate from DMs.
An OpenAI-compatible server (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses with stored history, /v1/models) with streaming so any compatible frontend can chat with the agent.
API: one port serving several agent profiles
Each profile is served under its own URL prefix with its own response store.
Long agent runs are admitted durably with status, event streams, cancel and idempotency keys.
Webhooks: signed routes that trigger agent runs
HMAC-validated routes (GitHub, GitLab, Linear, generic) filter and transform payloads into prompts, can deliver directly or fire a scheduled job, and send results to any chat.
Bursts of events on one entity dispatch only the latest after a quiet window.
Graph change notifications (with validation handshake) arrive as gateway events.
Any backend can push messages in via a signed webhook and receive replies on a signed callback, with idempotency and ordered sequence numbers; external systems can also post into channels.
A script-tag chat widget per bot with allowed domains, optional Turnstile check, history, reset and feedback.
A real-time WebSocket channel with per-connection conversations, streaming, history and reconnect hydration, used by web and terminal clients.
An interactive terminal channel that streams text, thinking and tool calls with colours.
Chat-app setup copy and Save step (Who answers, Who may message it)

The setup wizard's Save step asks 'Who answers in <app>' (default Trunk) and 'Who may message it' (Only me, People I approve, Anyone in my workspace); errors for a malformed token don't blame the app; honest prerequisites and times; empty Paste steps skipped.
/trunk shows which Trunk answers in this chat; the owner's DM can switch it, and '/trunk name message' talks to one named Trunk without re-routing.
In groups, progress shows counts and kinds only, never names, files or commands; summaries stay private.
Never show a streamed secret half-typed
Streaming buffers the trailing word so a secret is never visible part-typed before redaction.
Chat permissions under the owner's standing rules
Chat commands respect the owner's Full Access standing rules and per-sender permissions without standing consent; extra chat permissions are an explicit list.
